	**1901** में, **रवींद्रनाथ टैगोर** ने शांतिनिकेतन में **ब्रह्मचर्य आश्रम** (बाद में **पाठ भवन**) नामक एक प्रयोगात्मक विद्यालय की स्थापना की, जो **खुली हवा में शिक्षा** और प्रकृति के माध्यम से सीखने के सिद्धांतों पर आधारित था।
	टैगोर ने **1921** में इस संस्थान का विस्तार **विश्व-भारती विश्वविद्यालय** के रूप में किया, जिसकी कल्पना उन्होंने एक ऐसे विश्व केंद्र के रूप में की थी जहाँ सांस्कृतिक और शैक्षणिक आदान-प्रदान के माध्यम से **पूर्व** और **पश्चिम** का मिलन हो सके।
	इस संस्थान को **1951** में **भारतीय संसद** के एक अधिनियम द्वारा एक **केंद्रीय विश्वविद्यालय** और **राष्ट्रीय महत्व का संस्थान** घोषित किया गया था।
	**सितंबर 2023** में, **शांतिनिकेतन** को **अंतर्राष्ट्रीयतावाद** और **मानवतावाद** के प्रति इसके अनूठे दृष्टिकोण को मान्यता देते हुए **भारत के 41वें यूनेस्को (UNESCO) विश्व धरोहर स्थल** के रूप में शामिल किया गया था।

 **Additional Information**

	**प्रांतीय महाविद्यालय**:

	
		**1817** में **कलकत्ता** में **हिंदू **महाविद्यालय के रूप में स्थापित, इसका नाम बदलकर **1855** में **प्रांतीय महाविद्यालय** कर दिया गया और बाद में **2010** में इसे प्रांतीय महाविद्यालय के रूप में उन्नत किया गया।
	
	
	**फोर्ट विलियम **महाविद्यालय :
	
		इसकी स्थापना **1800** में **भारत के गवर्नर-जनरल** **लॉर्ड वेलेज़ली** द्वारा ब्रिटिश सिविल सेवकों को **भारतीय भाषाओं**, **रीति-रिवाजों** और **कानून** में प्रशिक्षित करने के लिए की गई थी।
	
	
	**हिंदू **महाविद्यालय :
	
		भारतीय जनता के बीच **आधुनिक पश्चिमी शिक्षा** को बढ़ावा देने के लिए **1817** में **कलकत्ता** में **राजा राम मोहन राय**, **डेविड हेयर** और **राधाकांत देव** द्वारा स्थापित किया गया था।

questions.questionText: Which revolutionary freedom fighter is popularly remembered as “Shaheed-e-Azam”?
questions.questionTextHi: किस क्रांतिकारी स्वतंत्रता सेनानी को लोकप्रिय रूप से "शहीद-ए-आजम" के रूप में याद किया जाता है?
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is **Bhagat Singh**.

**Key Points**

	**Bhagat Singh** was a charismatic Indian revolutionary who became an enduring symbol of resistance against British colonial rule. He was born on **September 28, 1907**, in the village of **Banga**, Punjab.
	The honorific title **Shaheed-e-Azam** (meaning **Great Martyr** or **King of Martyrs**) was bestowed upon him by the Indian public to honor his supreme sacrifice for the nation at the young age of **23**.
	He was a leading figure in the **Hindustan Socialist Republican Association (HSRA)**, where he worked to transform the revolutionary movement from individual acts of heroism to a broader struggle based on **socialist ideology**.
	Singh was convicted in the **Lahore Conspiracy Case** for the assassination of British police officer **John Saunders** in **1928**. This act was carried out as retaliation for the death of the veteran leader **Lala Lajpat Rai**.
	On **April 8, 1929**, he and **Batukeshwar Dutt** threw non-lethal smoke bombs into the **Central Legislative Assembly** in Delhi to protest against the **Public Safety Bill** and the **Trade Dispute Bill**, raising the legendary slogan **Inquilab Zindabad**.
	He was executed by hanging on **March 23, 1931**, in the **Lahore Jail** alongside **Sukhdev** and **Rajguru**. This day is observed as **Shaheed Diwas** (Martyrs Day) across India.

 **Additional Information**

	**Lala Lajpat Rai**:

	
		Known as **Punjab Kesari** (Lion of Punjab), he was a prominent leader of the **Lal-Bal-Pal** trio within the **Indian National Congress**. He passed away in **November 1928** after being severely injured during a protest against the **Simon Commission**.
	
	
	**Chandrashekhar Azad**:
	
		A fearless revolutionary and the commander-in-chief of the **HSRA**. He maintained his vow of remaining **Azad** (free) and died during a fierce shootout with the police at **Alfred Park**, Allahabad, in **February 1931**.
	
	
	**Abbas Ali**:
	
		A dedicated Indian freedom fighter and a captain in the **Indian National Army (INA)** led by **Subhas Chandra Bose**. He was heavily influenced by the revolutionary ideas of **Bhagat Singh** and was a lifelong advocate for socialist principles.
questions.explanationHi:
सही उत्तर **भगत सिंह** है।

**Key Points**

	**भगत सिंह** एक करिश्माई भारतीय क्रांतिकारी थे जो ब्रिटिश औपनिवेशिक शासन के खिलाफ प्रतिरोध के एक स्थायी प्रतीक बन गए। उनका जन्म **28 सितंबर, 1907** को पंजाब के **बंगा** गाँव में हुआ था।
	भारतीय जनता द्वारा उन्हें मात्र **23** वर्ष की अल्पायु में देश के लिए दिए गए सर्वोच्च बलिदान के सम्मान में मानद उपाधि **शहीद-ए-आजम** (अर्थात **महान शहीद** या **शहीदों के राजा**) प्रदान की गई थी।
	वह **हिंदुस्तान समाजवादी गणराज्य संघ**** (HSRA)** के एक प्रमुख नेता थे, जहाँ उन्होंने क्रांतिकारी आंदोलन को व्यक्तिगत वीरता के कृत्यों से बदलकर **समाजवादी विचारधारा** पर आधारित एक व्यापक संघर्ष में बदलने का काम किया।
	सिंह को **1928** में ब्रिटिश पुलिस अधिकारी **जॉन सॉन्डर्स** की हत्या के लिए **लाहौर षड़यंत्र मामले** में दोषी ठहराया गया था। यह कृत्य अनुभवी नेता **लाला लाजपत राय** की मृत्यु के प्रतिशोध के रूप में किया गया था।
	**8 अप्रैल, 1929** को, उन्होंने और **बटुकेश्वर दत्त** ने लोक सुरक्षा विधेयक और श्रमिक विवाद विधेयक के विरोध में दिल्ली की केंद्रीय विधान सभा में अहानिकर धूम्र बम फेंके तथा प्रसिद्ध उद्घोष “इंकलाब ज़िंदाबाद” बुलंद किया।
	उन्हें **23 मार्च, 1931** को **लाहौर जेल** में **सुखदेव** और **राजगुरु** के साथ फांसी दे दी गई थी। इस दिन को पूरे भारत में **शहीद दिवस** के रूप में मनाया जाता है।

 **Additional Information**

	**लाला लाजपत राय**:

	
		उन्हें **पंजाब केसरी** (पंजाब का शेर) के रूप में जाना जाता था, वह **भारतीय राष्ट्रीय कांग्रेस** के भीतर **लाल-बाल-पाल** तिकड़ी के एक प्रमुख नेता थे। **साइमन कमीशन** के खिलाफ एक विरोध प्रदर्शन के दौरान गंभीर रूप से घायल होने के बाद **नवंबर 1928** में उनका निधन हो गया था।
	
	
	**चन्द्रशेखर आज़ाद**:
	
		एक निडर क्रांतिकारी और **HSRA** के प्रधान सेनापति थे। उन्होंने **आज़ाद** (मुक्त) रहने के अपने संकल्प को बनाए रखा और **फरवरी 1931** में इलाहाबाद के **अल्फ्रेड पार्क** में पुलिस के साथ एक भीषण मुठभेड़ के दौरान वीरगति को प्राप्त हुए।
	
	
	**अब्बास अली**:
	
		एक समर्पित भारतीय स्वतंत्रता सेनानी और **सुभाष चंद्र बोस** के नेतृत्व वाली **आजाद हिंद फौज (INA)** में कैप्टन थे। वे **भगत सिंह** के क्रांतिकारी विचारों से अत्यधिक प्रभावित थे और जीवन भर समाजवादी सिद्धांतों के समर्थक रहे।

questions.questionText: Choose the word that is most opposite in meaning to **“Delay”**.

    The word **"Hasten"** means to move or act quickly, or to cause something to happen sooner. (शीघ्रता करना)
    
        **Example:** The doctor hastened to the patient’s bedside when he heard the emergency call.
    
    Since "Hasten" is the opposite of "Delay," it is the correct answer.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Hasten**.

**Additional Information**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

        **Example:** The meeting was postponed to next week due to scheduling conflicts.
    
    
    **Defer** (टालना): To delay or put off an action or decision to a later time.
    
        **Example:** The committee decided to defer the final decision until more information was available.
    
    
    **Procrastinate** (टालमटोल करना): To delay or postpone an action unnecessarily, often due to laziness or fear of the task.
    
        **Example:** He procrastinated on finishing his project until the night before it was due.

questions.questionText:
Which of the following options is the most suitable conversion of the following sentence into Passive Voice?

The traffic department implements new traffic laws to reduce congestion.

options.text: New traffic laws were implemented by the traffic department to reduce congestion.
New traffic laws are being implemented by the traffic department to reduce congestion.
New traffic laws have been implemented by the traffic department to reduce congestion.
New traffic laws are implemented by the traffic department to reduce congestion.

questions.explanation:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

**Key Points**

	The given sentence is in the **Simple Present Tense** in the active voice.
	The structure for **Active Voice** in Simple Present is: **Subject + Verb (s/es) + Object.**
	The structure for **Passive Voice** in Simple Present is: **Object + am/is/are + Past Participle (V3) + by + Subject.**
	In the active voice: 
	
		**Subject:** The traffic department
		**Verb:** implements
		**Object:** new traffic laws
	
	 
	To convert to passive: 
	
		The object **"new traffic laws"** (plural) moves to the subject position.
		Because the subject is plural, we use the auxiliary verb **"are."**
		The verb "implements" changes to its V3 form, **"implemented."**
		The original subject is added after **"by."**
	
	 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"New traffic laws are implemented by the traffic department to reduce congestion."*

 

**Additional Information**

	**Option 1: **"New traffic laws were implemented..." – Incorrect because "were" is used for the **Simple Past Tense**.
	**Option 2: **"New traffic laws are being implemented..." – Incorrect because "are being" is used for the **Present Continuous Tense**.
	**Option 3: **"New traffic laws have been implemented..." – Incorrect because "have been" is used for the **Present Perfect Tense**.

questions.questionText:
Which of the following options is the most suitable conversion of the following sentence into Passive Voice?

Why did the baker add salt to the cake batter?

options.text: Why is salt added to the cake batter by the baker?
Why are salt added to the cake batter by the baker?
Why was salt added to the cake batter by the baker?
Why did salt added to the cake batter by the baker?

questions.explanation:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Key Points**

	The given sentence is in the **Simple Past Tense** in the active voice and is an interrogative sentence starting with "Why."
	The structure for **Active Voice** (Simple Past Interrogative) is: **Wh-word + did + Subject + Base Verb (V1) + Object?**
	The structure for **Passive Voice** (Simple Past Interrogative) is: **Wh-word + was/were + Object + Past Participle (V3) + by + Subject?**
	In the active voice: 
	
		**Subject:** the baker
		**Verb:** add
		**Object:** salt
	
	 
	To convert to passive: 
	
		The interrogative word **"Why"** remains at the beginning.
		The object **"salt"** becomes the new subject. Since "salt" is uncountable/singular, we use the auxiliary verb **"was."**
		The verb "add" changes to its V3 form, **"added."**
		The agent **"by the baker"** is added at the end.
	
	 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"Why was salt added to the cake batter by the baker?"*

 

**Additional Information**

	**Option 1: **"Why is salt added..." – Incorrect because "is" is used for the **Simple Present Tense**.
	**Option 2: **"Why are salt added..." – Incorrect because "are" is the plural present auxiliary; "salt" is singular and the tense should be past.
	**Option 4: **"Why did salt added..." – Grammatically incorrect construction. "Did" is an active voice auxiliary and cannot be paired with the V3 form "added" in this way.

questions.questionText:
Which of the following options is the most suitable conversion of the following sentence into active voice?

Major breakthroughs in renewable energy have been achieved by scientists in recent decades.

options.text: Scientists achieve major breakthroughs in renewable energy in recent decades.
Scientists are achieving major breakthroughs in renewable energy in recent decades.
Scientists achieved major breakthroughs in renewable energy in recent decades.
Scientists have achieved major breakthroughs in renewable energy in recent decades.

questions.explanation:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

**Key Points**

	The given sentence is in the **Passive Voice** of the **Present Perfect Tense**.
	Passive voice structure for Present Perfect: **Object + has/have + been + Past Participle (V3) + by + Subject.**
	To convert it into the **Active Voice**, the structure should be: **Subject + has/have + Past Participle (V3) + Object.**
	The agent in the passive sentence "scientists" becomes the subject of the active sentence.
	The verb phrase "have been achieved" changes to its active form **"have achieved"** to maintain the same tense.
	The phrase "in recent decades" remains at the end of the sentence to indicate the time frame.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"Scientists have achieved major breakthroughs in renewable energy in recent decades."*

 

**Additional Information**

	**Option 1: **"Scientists achieve..." – Incorrect because it changes the tense to **Simple Present**.
	**Option 2: **"Scientists are achieving..." – Incorrect because it changes the tense to **Present Continuous**.
	**Option 3: **"Scientists achieved..." – Incorrect because it changes the tense to **Simple Past**.

questions.questionText:
Which of the following options is the most suitable conversion of the following sentence into active voice?

By whom has this programme been authorised?

options.text: This programme has been authorised by whom?
By who is this programme authorised?

questions.explanation:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Key Points**

	The given sentence is in the **Passive Voice** of the **Present Perfect Tense** and is an interrogative sentence starting with "By whom."
	Passive voice structure for Present Perfect (Interrogative with 'By whom'): **By whom + has/have + Object + been + Past Participle (V3)?**
	To convert it into the **Active Voice**, the structure should be: **Who + has/have + Past Participle (V3) + Object?**
	In the transformation: 
	
		**"By whom"** changes to **"Who"** (the subject pronoun).
		The auxiliary **"has been authorised"** (passive) changes to **"has authorised"** (active).
		The subject of the passive sentence, **"this programme,"** becomes the object of the active sentence.
	
	 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"Who has authorised this programme?"*

 

**Additional Information**

	**Option 2: **"Whom has authorised..." – Incorrect because **"Whom"** is an object pronoun and cannot function as the subject of the sentence.
	**Option 3: **"This programme has been authorised by whom?" – Incorrect because this is still the **Passive Voice**, simply rearranged.
	**Option 4: **"By who is this programme authorised?" – Incorrect because it changes the tense to **Simple Present** and uses "who" incorrectly after a preposition (it should be "by whom" if passive).

questions.questionText:

The crops are infested ________ exotic pests unknown to this land.

    **Option 1 (by)** is incorrect because it implies an agent performing an action, which does not fit the context.
    **Option 2 (along)** is incorrect as it indicates movement or position, which is not applicable here.
    **Option 4 (for)** is incorrect because it implies purpose or intention, which does not apply to the infestation.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Complete Sentence:** *"The crops are infested **with** exotic pests unknown to this land."*

 

**Additional Information**

    **Option 1: "by"** is used to indicate the agent performing an action, which is not the intent in this sentence.
    **Option 2: "along"** is used to indicate direction or position, which is irrelevant to this context.
    **Option 4: "for"** is used to indicate purpose or benefit, which does not align with the meaning of the sentence.

questions.questionText:
A part of the following sentence is underlined. Choose the option which can replace the underlined part to improve the sentence. In case Options A, B and C are not found suitable, choose Option D: “No Improvement Required.”

The report suggested that unless corrective steps are taken immediately, **the problem would aggravate into** an uncontrollable crisis.
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is '**3**' i.e. 'the problem would escalate into'.
 
 
 
**Key Points**
 
 
    The word "**aggravate**" is incorrect in this context because it means to worsen a situation, but it does not imply a progression into a crisis. 
    The correct verb to use here is "**escalate**," which means to increase or intensify, and fits the context of the problem turning into an uncontrollable crisis. 
    **Option 1: "the problem would alleviate"** is incorrect because "alleviate" means to reduce or ease a problem, which is opposite to the intended meaning. 
    **Option 2: "the problem will retaliate with"** is incorrect because "retaliate" means to respond aggressively, which does not fit the scenario described. 
    **Option 4: "No improvement required"** is incorrect because the original sentence uses "aggravate," which is not the correct choice of word in this context. 
 
Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.
 
 
 
**Complete Sentence:** *"The report suggested that unless corrective steps are taken immediately, the problem **would escalate into** an uncontrollable crisis."*
 
 
 
**Additional Information**
 
 
    **Option 1: "the problem would alleviate"** is incorrect because "alleviate" means to reduce a problem, which contradicts the idea of escalation. 
    **Option 2: "the problem will retaliate with"** is incorrect because "retaliate" implies an aggressive response, which does not suit the context. 
    **Option 4: No improvement required** is incorrect because the original sentence uses the word "aggravate," which is not appropriate in this context.

The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Key Points**

    The paragraph focuses on Ralph's unclear goals during college and his struggles with self-discovery.
    **Sentence B is the first in the sequence** because it introduces Ralph's initial aspirations and his realization that he lacked the qualities needed for certain professions:
        
            "He first thought he wanted to be a doctor, or a lawyer, and he took pre-medical courses and courses in history of jurisprudence and business-law before he decided he had neither the emotional detachment necessary for medicine, nor the ability for sustained reading and memorization in the Corpus Iuris Civilis, as well as the more modern texts on property and inheritance."
        
    
    **Sentence A follows** as it describes his continued indecisiveness and exploration of various subjects:
        
            "Though he continued to take classes here and there in the sciences and in the Department of Business, he also took some lower-division classes in history and philosophy and English."
        
    
    **Sentence D is the third sentence** as it reflects Ralph's internal struggle and his feeling of being on the verge of a significant realization about himself:
        
            "He continually felt he was on the brink of some kind of momentous discovery about himself."
        
    
    **Sentence C is the last** as it concludes that the anticipated discovery never happened:
        
            "But it never came."
        
    
    The correct sequence is **BADC**.

 

**Coherent paragraph after rearrangement**:

"He first thought he wanted to be a doctor, or a lawyer, and he took pre-medical courses and courses in history of jurisprudence and business-law before he decided he had neither the emotional detachment necessary for medicine, nor the ability for sustained reading and memorization in the Corpus Iuris Civilis, as well as the more modern texts on property and inheritance. Though he continued to take classes here and there in the sciences and in the Department of Business, he also took some lower-division classes in history and philosophy and English. He continually felt he was on the brink of some kind of momentous discovery about himself. But it never came."

questions.questionText:

The other four sentences between the first and last sentences are jumbled up and are numbered A, B, C, and D. S1. There was plenty of fish in the creek, fresh-water bream, cod, cat-fish, and tailers.
A. Andy would fish for three hours at a stretch if encouraged by a 'nibble' or a 'bite' now and then - say once in twenty minutes.

C. However, the creek was low, just a chain of muddy water-holes, from the hole with a few bucketfuls in it to the sizable pool with an average depth of six or seven feet, and they could get fish by baling out the smaller holes or muddying up the water in the larger ones till the fish rose to the surface.
D. The butcher was always willing to give meat in exchange for fish when they caught more than they could eat; but now it was winter, and these fish wouldn't bite.
S2. There was the cat-fish, with spikes growing out of the sides of its head, and if you got pricked you'd know it, as Dave said.
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Key Points**

    The paragraph starts with S1, which introduces the setting by describing the abundance of fish in the creek.
    **Sentence B follows** as it introduces the characters (Andy and Dave) and their fondness for fishing, which directly connects to the first sentence: 
        
            "The party were fond of fish, and Andy and Dave of fishing."
        
    
    **Sentence A is next** because it elaborates on Andy’s fishing habits, which aligns logically after introducing the characters: 
        
            "Andy would fish for three hours at a stretch if encouraged by a 'nibble' or a 'bite' now and then - say once in twenty minutes."
        
    
    **Sentence D follows** as it describes the challenges of fishing in winter and the barter system with the butcher, providing context to the fishing dynamics: 
        
            "The butcher was always willing to give meat in exchange for fish when they caught more than they could eat; but now it was winter, and these fish wouldn't bite."
        
    
    **Sentence C comes next**, as it explains how they managed to catch fish despite the low creek levels, providing a solution to the challenges described in Sentence D: 
        
            "However, the creek was low, just a chain of muddy water-holes, from the hole with a few bucketfuls in it to the sizable pool with an average depth of six or seven feet, and they could get fish by baling out the smaller holes or muddying up the water in the larger ones till the fish rose to the surface."
        
    
    The paragraph ends with S2, which concludes by describing the cat-fish and its distinctive characteristics.

questions.questionText:
Given below are six sentences taken from a paragraph. The first and the last sentences are numbered S1 and S2 and are placed in the first and last positions respectively and are fixed in their positions. The other four sentences between the first and last sentences are jumbled up and are numbered A, B, C, and D. Rearrange the jumbled sentences in a logical sequence keeping the unity and coherence of the paragraph intact. Choose the correct alternative that best describes the sequence.

S1. I was rich and contented; I found pleasure in everything that appeals to a man of thirty-five.
A. I married a year ago.
B. A very beautiful, kindly and cultured young lady was my wife.
C. It was a love match.
D. She had been a companion to a countess not far from my estate.
S2. She loved me, and her heart was full of gratitude.
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Key Points**

    The paragraph revolves around the narrator's life and his relationship with his wife, who is described as a cultured and loving partner.
    **Sentence A** introduces the marriage of the narrator, which is the starting point of the story.
    **Sentence C** follows as it indicates the nature of the marriage, which is described as a love match.
    **Sentence B** comes next as it describes the wife of the narrator, emphasizing her qualities.
    **Sentence D** concludes the sequence before S2 by providing information about the wife's background, which complements her introduction in Sentence B.
    The correct sequence is **ACBD**.

 

**Coherent paragraph after rearrangement**:

"I was rich and contented; I found pleasure in everything that appeals to a man of thirty-five. I married a year ago. It was a love match. A very beautiful, kindly and cultured young lady was my wife. She had been a companion to a countess not far from my estate. She loved me, and her heart was full of gratitude."

questions.questionText:
The following sentence is divided into four parts and are given in the alternatives A, B, C, and D. Select that alternative which contains that part of the sentence which has an error. Selecting the part with the error is the answer.

If you are looking for a free parking space, you might drive on for hours until you find one.
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Key Points**

	The error is found in **part C** of the sentence (Option 3).
	The phrasal verb "**drive on**" is used incorrectly in this context. It means to continue moving in the same direction or to resume a journey.
	When searching for something within an area, such as a parking spot, the correct phrasal verb is "**drive around**" or "**drive about**," which means to travel to different parts of a location.
	The sentence describes a search process, so "**might drive around for hours**" is the grammatically and contextually appropriate choice.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"If you are looking for a free parking space, you **might drive around for hours** until you find one."*

 

**Additional Information**

	**Option 1: "If you are looking for"** – This part is correct; the present continuous "are looking" appropriately describes an ongoing action or search.
	**Option 2: "a free parking space, you"** – This part is correct. "Parking space" is a singular countable noun requiring the article "a," and the comma correctly separates the "if" clause from the main clause.
	**Option 4: "until you find one."** – This part is correct. In time clauses (using until, when, etc.), the present simple ("find") is used to refer to the future. "One" is the correct pronoun referring back to "parking space."

questions.questionText:
Identify the correct verb form in the sentence.

“Calcium, on the other hand, ___ primarily associated with the formation and maintenance of strong bones and teeth.”
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is '**Option 4**'.

 

**Key Points**

	***Option 4: is***

	
		The subject of the sentence is **"Calcium"**.
		Calcium is an **uncountable (mass) noun**, which always takes a **singular verb**.
		The passage is written in the **simple present tense** to state scientific facts and general truths. Therefore, the singular present form of the verb "to be" (**is**) is the correct choice.
	
	
	***Option 1: are***
	
		This is **incorrect**. "Are" is the plural form and cannot be used with the singular noun "Calcium."
	
	
	***Option 2: had***
	
		This is **incorrect**. "Had" is a past tense auxiliary or possessive verb. It does not function as a linking verb in this context to describe a quality or association.
	
	
	***Option 3: was***
	
		This is **incorrect**. While "was" is singular, it is in the **past tense**. Since the passage discusses the ongoing biological functions of minerals, the present tense is required.
	
	

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4.**

 

**Additional Information**

	**Subject-Verb Agreement**: Mass nouns like *water, sugar, iron,* and *calcium* are treated as singular. (Example: *Iron **is** essential.*)
	**Biological Context**: 
	
		**Iron**: Necessary for **hemoglobin**, which carries oxygen in the blood. Deficiency leads to **anemia**.
		**Calcium**: Necessary for **bone density**. Deficiency leads to **osteoporosis**, especially in women.
	
	
	**Vocabulary**: 
	
		**Indispensable**: Absolutely necessary.
		**Imperative**: Of vital importance; crucial.

questions.questionText:
Identify the type of sentence.

“A deficiency of iron often leads to anemia.”
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is '**Option 3**'.

 

**Key Points**

	***Option 3: Declarative***

	
		A **declarative sentence** is used to make a statement, provide a fact, offer an explanation, or convey information.
		The sentence *"A deficiency of iron often leads to anemia"* is stating a scientific fact about human health.
		Declarative sentences always end with a **period (full stop)**. They are the "workhorses" of writing, simply declaring how things are.
	
	
	***Option 1: Exclamatory***
	
		This is **incorrect**. Exclamatory sentences express strong emotion or surprise and must end with an **exclamation mark (!)** (e.g., *"How vital iron is for our survival!"*).
	
	
	***Option 2: Interrogative***
	
		This is **incorrect**. Interrogative sentences ask a direct question and end with a **question mark (?)** (e.g., *"Does iron deficiency cause fatigue?"*).
	
	
	***Option 4: Imperative***
	
		This is **incorrect**. Imperative sentences give a command, a request, or an instruction. They often omit the subject "you" (e.g., *"Eat more green leafy vegetables to prevent anemia."*).
	
	

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3.**

 

**Additional Information**

	**Sentence Functions**: Most formal writing (like the passage on iron and calcium) relies heavily on declarative sentences because they are the most effective way to transmit data and logical arguments.
	**Grammar Note**: Even though "leads" is the verb here, the entire sentence functions as a single declaration. 
	**Vocabulary Connection**: The word **"deficiency"** means a lack or shortage. In this declarative context, it is the subject of the sentence that "leads" to the result (anemia).

questions.questionText: The word ‘indispensable’ in the sentence “Iron and calcium are two indispensable minerals required for the healthy growth of the human body...” means ________.
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is '**Option 2**'.

 

**Key Points**

	***Option 2: essential***

	
		In the context of the sentence, **"indispensable"** describes minerals that are **"required for the healthy growth of the human body."**
		The word "indispensable" means absolutely necessary, essential, or something that cannot be done without.
		If a substance is "required" for health, it is by definition **essential** to the body's functioning.
	
	
	***Option 1: harmful***
	
		This is **incorrect**. "Harmful" would mean the minerals cause damage, which contradicts the statement that they are needed for "healthy growth."
	
	
	***Option 3: temporary***
	
		This is **incorrect**. "Temporary" refers to something that lasts for a limited time, which does not fit the description of a fundamental requirement for growth.
	
	
	***Option 4: avoidable***
	
		This is **incorrect**. "Avoidable" is an antonym (opposite) of indispensable. If something is required, it cannot be avoided if one wishes to remain healthy.
	
	

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2.**

 

**Additional Information**

	**Etymology**: The word comes from the prefix **"in-"** (meaning "not") + **"dispensable"** (meaning "able to be set aside or done without"). Combined, it means "not able to be set aside."
	**Synonyms**: Crucial, vital, necessary, imperative, requisite.
	**Contextual Usage**: In nutrition, "essential" minerals are those the body cannot produce on its own and must obtain from the diet. Iron and calcium fall into this "indispensable" category because they are structural and functional cornerstones of human biology.

questions.questionText: In the sentence “...in women it increases the risk of osteoporosis—a condition where bones become porous and fragile,” the antonym of ‘fragile’ is ________.
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is '**Option 4**'.

 

**Key Points**

	***Option 4: strong***

	
		An **antonym** is a word that has the **opposite** meaning of another word.
		In the passage, **"fragile"** describes bones that are "porous" and easily broken or damaged due to a lack of density.
		**"Strong"** is the direct opposite, as it refers to something that is powerful, sturdy, and able to withstand pressure without breaking.
	
	
	***Option 1, 2, & 3: weak, delicate, and brittle***
	
		These words are **synonyms** (words with similar meanings) of fragile.
		**Weak**: Lacking physical strength.
		**Delicate**: Very fine in texture or easily broken.
		**Brittle**: Hard but liable to shatter easily.
	
	

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4.**

 

**Additional Information**

Shutterstock Explore

	**Context Clues**: The sentence uses the word "porous" (full of holes) to define the condition. In a building or a bone, a structure with more holes is "fragile," while a dense, solid structure is **strong**.
	**Osteoporosis**: This condition literally translates to "porous bones." It highlights the importance of **calcium** in maintaining a "strong" skeletal system.
	**Vocabulary Tip**: When faced with a question asking for an antonym, look at the group of words provided. If three options (weak, delicate, brittle) share a similar theme of "easiness to break," the outlier (strong) is almost certainly the correct opposite.

questions.questionText: According to the passage, why do “pregnant and lactating mothers require additional calcium”?

options.text: Because of their role in household work
Because their bodies support both their own needs and those of the growing child

questions.explanation:
The correct answer is '**Option 3**'.

 

**Key Points**

	***Option 3: Because their bodies support both their own needs and those of the growing child***

	
		The passage explicitly states: **"Pregnant and lactating mothers require additional calcium, as their bodies support not only their own needs but also those of the growing child."**
		During pregnancy, the mother's body must provide enough calcium to develop the **skeletal system** of the fetus.
		During lactation (breastfeeding), the mother loses calcium through her milk, which is essential for the **infant's bone growth** and development.
	
	
	***Option 1: Because they eat less food***
	
		This is **incorrect**. The passage does not mention food quantity for mothers, but rather the increased **nutritional demand** placed on their bodies.
	
	
	***Option 2: Because of their role in household work***
	
		This is **incorrect**. While physical activity can influence health, the passage links the need for calcium to **biological support** for the child, not physical labor.
	
	
	***Option 4: Because they avoid dairy products***
	
		This is **incorrect**. The passage suggests that a *lack* of dairy products contributes to deficiency, but it does not say that mothers specifically avoid them.
	
	

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3.**

 

**Additional Information**

	**Calcium and Bone Density**: If a mother does not consume enough calcium, her body will actually **leach calcium from her own bones** to provide for the baby, increasing her risk of osteoporosis later in life.
	**Lactation**: A lactating mother provides approximately 200–300 mg of calcium per day to her infant through breast milk, making daily **replenishment** critical.
	**Nutritional Synergy**: Vitamin D is often required alongside calcium to ensure the body can effectively **absorb** the mineral into the bones.
